howWeCheck.title: How we check job postings
howWeCheck.subtitle: Only the editorial team assigns a verification status. It cannot be bought: paying for promotion changes a job's reach, not its badge.
howWeCheck.levelsText: The badge on a card answers one question: how far we have got in checking that particular job.
howWeCheck.stepsTitle: What we do, step by step
howWeCheck.step1Title: We find the job in an official source
howWeCheck.step1Text: Sweden — Platsbanken/JobTech Arbetsförmedlingen, Norway — NAV. We show the link to the original on the card, and applications go there too.
howWeCheck.step1Note: Norwegian vacancies come from NAV's official database — arbeidsplassen.nav.no. A one-off measurement of our target segment on 24 August 2026 found that 33.4% of listings were unavailable through the feed because they were posted only on Finn.no. With a 60-day import window, we cover 54.4% of the total target segment. When looking for work in Norway, check Finn.no separately.
howWeCheck.step2Text: We cross-check the name against the company register (Bolagsverket, Brønnøysund). If an intermediary rather than the employer is behind the posting, we say so.
howWeCheck.step3Title: We break the terms down one by one
howWeCheck.step3Text: Pay (net or gross), housing, travel, hours, collective agreement. Every field separately; we mark the unknown as unknown, not as «by agreement».
howWeCheck.step4Text: If someone from the Baltics actually worked at the site and confirmed the terms, the job gets the top status. The editorial team verifies the review.
howWeCheck.limitsTitle: What we do not do and do not promise
howWeCheck.limit1: We take no payment from workers — not for access, not for applying, not for «priority».
howWeCheck.limit2: We do not accept candidates' documents: applications go directly to the official source.
howWeCheck.limit3: We do not raise verification status for money — that path does not exist even in the database structure.
howWeCheck.limit4: We do not guarantee employment, a visa, a tax outcome or a level of income. We explain the published terms and point you to the original source.
howWeCheck.workerNoteBefore: Have you worked in Sweden or Norway and want to confirm the terms?
howWeCheck.workerNoteAfter: — that is how the «Confirmed by a worker» status appears.

about.title: Who is behind BalticWorkers Check
about.subtitle: A Latvian company, not an anonymous website. Real people who translate and verify Scandinavian job listings for Baltic workers.
about.whoText: BalticWorkers Check is a project by SIA GELVUA, registered in Riga, Latvia. Managing director: Šakro Toliašvili.
about.whoText2: We are not a recruitment agency and not an intermediary. We display vacancies already published on official government databases — Arbeidsplassen (NAV, Norway) and Platsbanken (Arbetsförmedlingen, Sweden) — and translate their conditions into languages understood by workers from Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia.
about.whyText: A person from the Baltics moving to work in Scandinavia usually doesn't know three things: what they are legally entitled to be paid, who covers housing and travel, and who their employer actually is. An ad in Swedish or Norwegian rarely answers these questions — it is written for locals who don't need to relocate.
about.whyText2: We collect what is known and honestly flag what isn't.
about.dontItem1: We do not charge job seekers — not for access to listings, not for anything else. This is both our principle and a requirement of Latvian law governing employment services.
about.dontItem2: We do not submit applications on your behalf — you apply yourself, on the source's official site.
about.dontItem3: We do not sell listing placements to job seekers and do not promise employment.
about.dontItem4: We do not collect or store your personal data beyond what you provide yourself when subscribing to alerts.

yourRights.title: What's worth knowing before you go
yourRights.subtitle: Not legal advice — signposts to official sources. Every claim links to a primary source.
yourRights.feesTitle: No one has the right to charge you before work starts
yourRights.feesText1: No honest employer in the EU asks a worker for money upfront — not a deposit "to guarantee arrival," not a processing fee, not an advance for housing. If asked, it's fraud.
yourRights.feesText2: Latvian intermediaries are directly prohibited by law from charging job seekers for employment services (the Law on Support for the Unemployed and Job Seekers, Article 17, para. 9). Licensed companies are listed on the NVA website — if a company promises work abroad, check it there.
yourRights.feesLinkNva: NVA's list of licensed employment agencies ↗
yourRights.feesLinkLaw: Law on Support for the Unemployed and Job Seekers, Art. 17 ↗
yourRights.minimumTitle: Norway has a statutory minimum wage
yourRights.minimumText1: In a number of industries, the allmenngjøring mechanism applies: the terms of the collective agreement become mandatory for every employer in the industry, including foreign companies. Paying less is not allowed even if the employer isn't party to any agreement.
yourRights.minimumText2: This covers, among others, construction, cleaning, and the hotel and restaurant industry. Current rates are on the Arbeidstilsynet website.
yourRights.minimumText3: Reimbursement of travel, meals, and housing while on assignment is not part of the minimum rate: an employer may not pay below the minimum on the grounds that it covered your travel or housing.
yourRights.unionsTitle: You can join a union in the country where you work
yourRights.unionsText: This is the main thing Baltic workers almost never do — and it delivers the most.
yourRights.unionsText2: Scandinavian unions accept foreign workers. Membership provides legal help in a dispute with an employer, monitoring that the agreed rate is followed, and usually insurance. Dues are typically around one and a half percent of wages.
yourRights.unionsText3: You are not required to tell your employer that you're a union member.
yourRights.ifNotPaidSweden: Sweden — Arbetsmiljöverket, but for unpaid wages start with your industry union.
yourRights.ifNotPaidUnionNote: If you're a union member, start there: the union has lawyers and experience with exactly this kind of case.
yourRights.ifDifferentTitle: If conditions on the ground turned out different
yourRights.ifDifferentText: Write to us: baltworkers@gmail.com. We can't settle a dispute for you, but we'll correct the listing on the site so the next person knows the truth.
